title: Recurrent Neural Networks
overview: Recurrent networks process sequences one step at a time while carrying a hidden state. They share weights across time but struggle with long-range dependencies.
objectives: Unroll an RNN over a sequence

method.title: Hidden state
method.body: h_t = tanh(W_x x_t + W_h h_(t-1) + b) summarizes everything seen so far.

method.title: Weight sharing
method.body: The same parameters are applied at every time step, so sequence length can vary.

method.title: BPTT
method.body: Gradients are propagated back through the unrolled steps, multiplying by W_h repeatedly.

method.title: Gradient problems
method.body: Repeated multiplication makes gradients vanish or explode; clipping controls explosions.

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
Wx = rng.normal(size=(4, 8)) * 0.3
Wh = rng.normal(size=(8, 8)) * 0.3
h = np.zeros(8)
seq = rng.normal(size=(5, 4))
for t, x in enumerate(seq):
    h = np.tanh(x @ Wx + h @ Wh)
    print("step", t, "hidden norm", round(float(np.linalg.norm(h)), 3))
